name: scenario_0735
description: Allison is compiling research on demographic data across various topics and wants to extract specific age-related information from a set of charts to share with a colleague.

messages.content:
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}ROUND 1 [provide: image_1, image_2, image_3]
Query: Create a note called 'Age Demographics'. Look at these three charts, filter out the ones that contain demographic breakdowns by age, and add their main titles to the note.
Instructions: Instruct the assistant to create a note named 'Age Demographics' and add the main titles of the provided charts that include age-based demographic breakdowns. If the assistant asks what counts as an age breakdown, tell it to look for labels mentioning 'years old' or specific age ranges. Proceed to the next round once the note is created and populated with the correct titles.

ROUND 2 [provide: image_4, image_5, image_6]
Query: Here are three more charts. Apply the same filter: find the ones with age or generational breakdowns, and append their titles to the 'Age Demographics' note.
Instructions: Present the new charts and ask the assistant to apply the same filter, appending the titles of any charts with age or generational breakdowns to the 'Age Demographics' note. If the assistant includes a chart without age or generation data, correct it by pointing back to the images and asking it to look closer at the labels. Proceed when the note is successfully updated.

ROUND 3
Query: For the charts you identified that have age or generation breakdowns, extract the specific name of the youngest age group or generation listed in each, and append those names to the note next to their respective chart titles.
Instructions: Instruct the assistant to look back at the specific charts it filtered, identify the youngest age group or generation explicitly named in each of them, and add those group names to the note alongside their corresponding titles. If it misses one of the charts, remind it to check all the filtered ones. Proceed to the next round once done.

ROUND 4
Query: I want to share this research. Please email the contents of the 'Age Demographics' note to my colleague at the Institute with the subject 'Filtered Age Demographics Data'.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to email the contents of the 'Age Demographics' note to your colleague at the Institute, using the subject 'Filtered Age Demographics Data'. The assistant should find multiple colleagues at the Institute in your contacts and ask you to clarify which one. When it does, specify that you mean the one in the research department. Proceed once the email is sent.

ROUND 5
Query: Let's add some context for future reference. Search the web for the current age of Brett Kavanaugh (the political figure mentioned in one of our filtered charts), and append it to the end of the note.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to search the web for the current age of Brett Kavanaugh and append that age to the end of the 'Age Demographics' note. If the assistant asks for permission to perform the search, grant it. Conclude the conversation once the note has been successfully updated with his current age.

task_completion_criteria: Create a note named 'Age Demographics' containing the titles of the three charts with age or generational breakdowns ('The French are having second thoughts about Paris 2024', 'Favorability for Brett Kavanaugh, by group', and '7.2 Percent of U.S. Adults Identify as LGBT') along with the youngest age group or generation mentioned in each ('Under 35 years old', 'Men under 50' / 'Women under 50', and 'Gen Z').
